name: Canvas
description: A product README with open feature columns, compact sans hierarchy, a native options table and rounded architecture nodes.

references.name: Product Hero with Demo Panel
references.studied: A short centered headline, one broad visual field and an overlapping demonstration panel.

references.name: Bento Product Features
references.studied: Unequal cell sizes, varied visual content and a functional example inside each feature.

blocks.title: open-readme
blocks.subtitle:
Clear, designed READMEs.
Made for your coding agent.

items.title: Content comes first
items.description: Keep project facts, section order and design in one editable JSON file.

items.title: Control every section
items.description: Choose a complete system. Adjust a section’s style, typography or density when you need to.

items.title: Files you own
items.description: Local Markdown and light/dark SVGs. Commit the files; your README needs no image service.

blocks.title: Get started
blocks.code:
npm install --save-dev github:luc3xhj/open-readme#v0.4.0
npx open-readme init --project cli --design canvas
npx open-readme render --out README.preview.md --json
blocks.caption: Node.js 22+. Fill in your project’s facts, then render a preview.

blocks.title: Use with your agent
blocks.body:
Load the [agent skill](https://github.com/luc3xhj/open-readme/blob/main/skills/open-readme/SKILL.md), then ask:

> Design this repository’s README with open-readme. Verify the install and usage commands. Choose the useful sections, show me two complete design systems, and render to README.preview.md first.

Your agent inspects the repository, edits the config and runs the CLI. Review the result before replacing your README.

blocks.caption: Override the complete system or one block. Your content stays in the same config.

blocks.title: JavaScript API
blocks.caption: The CLI and browser use this same renderer. The output has no runtime dependency.

blocks.title: Works on GitHub
blocks.body:
Code, prose, references and links remain native Markdown. GitHub chooses light or dark SVGs automatically. Commit `README.md` and `assets/open-readme/` together.

Read the [configuration reference](https://github.com/luc3xhj/open-readme/blob/main/docs/configuration.md) and [section guide](https://github.com/luc3xhj/open-readme/blob/main/docs/sections.md).

blocks.title: Contribute
blocks.body: [Report an issue](https://github.com/luc3xhj/open-readme/issues) or read the [contribution guide](https://github.com/luc3xhj/open-readme/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). Design a section around a reader’s task, then check it within the complete README.

blocks.title: License & credits
blocks.body: [MIT](https://github.com/luc3xhj/open-readme/blob/main/LICENSE). Built by [Lucas](https://github.com/luc3xhj) at [Meridian Startups](https://meridianstartups.com). [Preview the complete designs](https://luc3xhj.github.io/open-readme/).

name: Console
description: A command manual with compact mono hierarchy, two-column entries, an aligned reference and a branching file tree.

references.name: TerminalBentoGrid
references.studied: A shared monospace rhythm, prompt markers, status labels and cells of different widths.

references.name: Code Block
references.studied: A file label, original line numbers, an emphasized command and a copyable source.

references.name: Feature Overview Bento
references.studied: A large serif statement, smaller supporting facts and a single hairline lattice instead of separated equal cards.

references.name: Editorial Collage Hero
